title: Participants are invited to design and develop **CAPACITY CONNECT A Digital Capacity Building and Learning Management Portal** to support organizational training, competency development, and knowledge sharing through a centralized web-based platform.
description: The solution should include secure signup and login functionality with three user roles: Trainee, Trainer, and Admin. Trainees should be able to create professional profiles with qualifications, work experience, interests, skills, and certificates, enroll in courses, access learning resources, attempt subject-wise MCQ assessments, and provide feedback on courses and training content.Trainers should be able to manage their profiles, create questionnaires with deadlines, monitor trainee participation and performance, and upload recorded lectures, presentations, and study materials in a trainer library accessible to trainees.The Admin module should provide user approval and role management features along with dashboards for monitoring courses, enrollments, certifications,assessments, and participation statistics. Admins should also be able to publish notifications, announcements, achievements, and newly added learning content on the homepage.The platform should support competency mapping for identifying suitable trainers for various subjects and should be scalable, secure, user-friendly, and accessible across devices to promote efficient learning and organizational capacity building.
summary: Innovation (2/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a smart education problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (4/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a working prototype is realistic in a 36-hour window. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Education. Tech Depth (1/5): centers on moderate engineering scope. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 15/30 -> Red verdict.

detail.title: CAPACITY CONNECT - Digital Capacity Building and Learning Management Portal

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a training portal with three user types, trainees, trainers, and admins, that handles course enrollment, assessments, content libraries, and organizational reporting all in one place.
overview.why_it_matters: A well-run training programme depends on tracking who's learning what and how well. A unified LMS makes that visible instead of scattered across emails and spreadsheets.
pain_points: No centralized platform for organizational training and competency development currently exists.
Trainee progress, certifications, and participation aren't systematically tracked.
No structured way to match trainers to subjects based on competency.
overview.background: Organizational training and capacity building currently lacks a centralized digital platform, making trainee tracking, learning analytics, and administration inefficient.
overview.whats_being_asked: A three-role (Trainee/Trainer/Admin) learning management portal with course enrollment, MCQ assessments, trainer content libraries, competency mapping, and admin dashboards.
expected_solution: Trainee profile, enrollment, and assessment functionality.
Trainer content management and trainee monitoring tools.
Admin dashboards for programme oversight and reporting.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Incremental. This is a standard multi-role LMS pattern, extremely well-established (many commercial and open-source LMS platforms exist), applied to a specific organizational context.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Very low. Standard CRUD, role-based access, and content-management functionality, minimal technical complexity.

competitive_landscape.level: Low crowding on this specific PS, but LMS platforms generally are extremely well-trodden
competitive_landscape.note: The pattern itself is one of the most common software categories in existence, differentiation depends entirely on execution and the competency-mapping feature specifically.

innovation.note: Extremely well-established LMS pattern, minimal conceptual novelty.

invention.note: Standard multi-role platform functionality, one of the most straightforward builds possible.

technical_feasibility.note: Fully achievable end to end with sample data, no dependencies of any kind.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine organizational value, but a familiar, unremarkable impact story relative to more specialized PS.

architecture.note: Standard three-role platform architecture, minimal integration risk.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Red, mainly due to very low innovation, this is one of the most generic, commonly-available software patterns possible (a basic LMS). Genuinely achievable but will struggle to stand out competitively without a specific, meaningful differentiator like genuinely useful competency-mapping intelligence.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Extremely low technical risk, fully buildable and polishable within 36 hours.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: This exact pattern (multi-role LMS) is available as commercial off-the-shelf software already, without a genuine differentiator, this submission risks reading as reinventing an existing wheel.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: If choosing this PS, commit to making the competency-mapping feature genuinely intelligent (matching trainers to subjects based on real skill/experience data, not just a manual tag list), that's the one part of this PS with real differentiation potential.

idea_0_4: Design your three-role system (Trainee/Trainer/Admin) with clear permission boundaries.
Decide your differentiator: intelligent competency-mapping (trainer-subject matching based on profile data) is the most promising angle.
Split: one person on core LMS functionality, one on the competency-mapping feature.
prototype_4_22: Build core trainee functionality: profile, enrollment, assessments.
Build trainer functionality: content upload, trainee monitoring, questionnaire creation.
Start your competency-mapping logic, matching trainer profiles to subject needs intelligently.
integration_22_30: Build admin functionality: user management, dashboards, notifications.
Connect all three roles into one coherent platform.
Test the competency-mapping feature with realistic sample trainer/subject data to confirm it produces sensible matches.
polish_30_36: Polish all three role-based interfaces for genuine usability.
Rehearse demoing the competency-mapping feature specifically as your differentiator.
Prepare to discuss why this isn't just an off-the-shelf LMS.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Demo your competency-mapping feature specifically, showing it intelligently matching a trainer profile to relevant subjects based on real skill/experience data, not a manual dropdown selection, that's the one genuinely differentiating element in this PS.

strengths: Very low technical risk, fully achievable in 36 hours.
Clear, well-specified feature requirements leave little ambiguity.
weaknesses: Extremely low innovation ceiling, one of the most generic software patterns in existence.
Genuine risk of reading as reinventing existing commercial LMS software without a real differentiator.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Weight toward the competency-mapping differentiator, that's what separates this from a generic LMS template.
team_fit.approach: Build core LMS functionality efficiently and quickly, then invest remaining time in making competency-mapping genuinely intelligent.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The entire standard LMS platform, this is one of the most well-trodden application patterns possible.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing a genuinely intelligent competency-mapping algorithm that reflects real trainer-subject fit, not just keyword matching, that's a thoughtful design decision.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded generic LMS without a genuine differentiator would be functionally complete but essentially indistinguishable from existing off-the-shelf platforms.

data_resource_availability.status: No dataset dependency, illustrative sample training/trainee data is sufficient for a demo.

judge_qna.question: Why build this instead of using an existing off-the-shelf LMS platform?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Lead with your competency-mapping differentiator specifically, and any organization-specific customization (cooperative/NCCT-relevant training categories), be direct that a generic LMS alone doesn't justify a custom build.
judge_qna.follow_up: What specific organizational need does your custom build address that an off-the-shelf LMS wouldn't?

judge_qna.question: How does your competency-mapping actually work, beyond simple tag matching?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through your specific matching logic, whether it factors in experience level, past training performance, or other signals beyond a manually selected subject tag.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would this handle a trainer with expertise spanning multiple subject areas?
